definitions.explanation: A small shop specializing in selling cigarettes, tobacco products, and often stamps and prepaid cards. A traditional feature of Japanese neighborhoods, though declining in number.

examples.english: There's a tobacco shop on the corner.

examples.japanese: たばこ{屋|や}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{切手|きって}→切手：00718_kitte⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{売|う}っている→売る：00906_uru⟧。
examples.english: They also sell stamps at the tobacco shop.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦どの→どの：00551_dono⟧⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧たばこ{屋|や}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦{代|か}わられている→代わる：11718_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: In the past every shopping street had a tobacco shop, but now they've been replaced by convenience stores.

notes:
A compound of ⟦たばこ→たばこ：02909_tabako⟧ (tobacco/cigarettes) + ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ (shop). Traditional たばこ{屋|や} are small, often family-run shops typically located at street corners. They were once ubiquitous in Japan and served as neighborhood landmarks and informal gathering spots.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- たばこ{屋|や}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧: the old lady at the tobacco shop
- ⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧たばこ{屋|や}: the neighborhood tobacco shop
- たばこ{屋|や}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy at the tobacco shop

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional たばこ{屋|や} also sell {収入印紙|しゅうにゅういんし} (revenue stamps), ⟦{切手|きって}→切手：00718_kitte⟧ (postage stamps), and ⟦{宝|たから}くじ→宝くじ：18549_takarakuji⟧ (lottery tickets). With the spread of convenience stores and vending machines, standalone tobacco shops have become increasingly rare, especially in urban areas.
